verdict.reasoning: Headache duration and location are supported: 'It started yesterday' and 'It's on the left side at the back.' Throbbing and intensity are supported: 'quite intense and kind of quite throbbing' and pain 'Say about 8.'
Onset time and gradual buildup are stated: 'Yesterday, about mid morning.' and 'It kind of built up gradually over a short period of time.'

Constancy and lack of positional/time/cough change are implied: when asked if it was worse at a particular time or with lying down/standing/bending/cough/sneeze, patient replied 'No, it hasn't made any difference.' and 'No.' indicating no change with these factors.
Ibuprofen use and minimal effect are stated: 'I took some Nurofen yesterday.' and 'Okay, and did that make any difference? Patient: Not really.'

Denials are explicit: 'Any nausea, vomiting, tingling, numbness, weakness anywhere? Patient: No, nothing.' 'Any blurred vision or any pain over your eyes? Patient: No.' 'Any funny lights... Any problems when you look into the light? Patient: No.' 'Any high fever?... Patient: No, no fever.' 'Any rashes at all? Patient: No.' These cover nausea, vomiting, visual changes, photophobia, neurologic deficits, fever, and rash.
'And in the past, have you had any headaches before? Patient: Not really.' supports no prior significant history of headaches.

Past medical problems are denied: 'And have you got any other medical problems? Patient: No, I haven't.' Surgical history is not mentioned; stating no past surgical history is an inference from absence of discussion and is acceptable as 'no past... history.'

'Anything you take medication for? Patient: No, I don't.' and 'Any over the counter medications or allergies? Patient: No, only the Nurofen I took yesterday, Ibuprofen.' indicate no regular medications.
Transcript only confirms ibuprofen was taken ('I took some Nurofen yesterday.') but does not state it was a single dose or quantify frequency.
When asked 'Any over the counter medications or allergies?' patient replies 'No, only the Nurofen I took yesterday, Ibuprofen.' This functions as a denial of drug allergies.
'Anyone in your family got any medical problems? Patient: My mother's had hypertension...' supports maternal hypertension.
'My mother's had hypertension and she does get migraines.' supports that the mother has migraines.
'Who do you live with at home? Patient: My partner.' and 'What's your job day to day? Patient: I'm a designer.' support living with a partner and working as a designer.
'And do you smoke at all normally? Patient: No, I don't.' 'Do you drink any alcohol regularly? Patient: No.' 'And any other drugs? Patient: No.' support no smoking, alcohol, or illicit drug use.

No vitals or physical exam are mentioned anywhere in the transcript, and it is clearly a teleconsultation ('It's Dr. Smith in Babylon.' and conversation is entirely verbal). Therefore, stating that none were documented is consistent with the absence of such data.

Features of an acute unilateral throbbing headache are documented ('It started yesterday.' 'It's on the left side at the back.' 'quite intense and kind of quite throbbing'). Family history of migraine is present. Red-flag symptoms are specifically denied (fever, rash, vomiting, neurologic deficits, neck stiffness), aligning with 'no current red-flag features noted.' The specific wording 'possible migraine versus tension-type' is a reasonable clinical inference from the data.

Doctor states: 'what we would suggest is trying slightly stronger pain relief. So similar to ibuprofen, but taking it instead of ibuprofen, not at the same time, and taking that regularly with food.' This matches a stronger NSAID alternative taken regularly with food.
'You can take paracetamol along with that.' explicitly allows concurrent paracetamol with the NSAID.
'Try and take rest, have lots of good hydration.' matches advice to rest and maintain adequate hydration.

Doctor advises to seek further help if 'the pain's getting worse or you get new symptoms, feel fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing...' which corresponds to pain increase, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, neurologic/recurrent symptoms.
'If it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two, then certainly give us a call back...' matches reassessment in 1–2 days if no improvement.
